title: Review: SI units and prefixes; Scalars and vectors; Density; Moments and static equilibrium; Systems and centre of mass; Newton's first law and equilibrium; Describing motion
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: FL01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D02-1#N.11, D07-1#N.5, D08-1#N.2, FL01-1#N.4, K01-1#N.2, MS01-1#N.12, MS05-1#N.4, D02-1#N.2, D07-1#N.7, D08-1#N.5a, FL01-1#N.9, K01-1#N.5. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Density
items.clue: Mass per unit volume; it belongs to the material, not to the object.

items.label: Equilibrium
items.clue: State of a body, such as a steadily falling skydiver, whose forces balance.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Runs from the first tail to the last tip when arrows are drawn tip to tail.

items.label: Terminal velocity
items.clue: Constant value a skydiver's downward motion settles at once drag equals weight.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.

questions.stem: A rectangular wooden sign hangs from a single hook through a hole at the middle of its top edge. A heavy metal letter is fixed near the sign's left end. How does the sign hang at rest?

options.text: Level, because the hook is at the middle of the top edge.
Tilted, left end lower, with its centre of gravity directly below the hook.
Tilted, left end lower, until the metal letter is directly below the hook.
Tilted, right end lower, to balance the heavy letter.

questions.explanation: At rest the weight has no moment about the hook, so its line of action passes through the hook. The sign turns until its centre of gravity, shifted left by the letter, is vertically below the hook.

questions.stem: A mechanic pulls with a 20 N force on the end of a tool handle, 0.25 m from the centre of a nut. The force is in the plane of the handle's turn, but at 30° to the handle instead of at 90°. What is the turning effect of the force about the centre of the nut?

options.text: 5.0 N m
4.3 N m
80 N m
2.5 N m

questions.explanation: Perpendicular distance = 0.25 × sin 30° = 0.125 m, so the turning effect = 20 × 0.125 = 2.5 N m.

questions.stem: The density of aluminium is 2.7 g cm⁻³. What is the volume, in m³, of an aluminium block of mass 0.081 kg?

A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns around and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?
Pressure is force ÷ area, and its unit is the pascal (Pa). What is the pascal in base units?

options.text: kg m s⁻²
kg m³ s⁻²
kg m⁻² s⁻²
kg m⁻¹ s⁻²

questions.explanation: Pa = N m⁻² = kg m s⁻² × m⁻² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.stem: A hiker walks 5 m east and then 9 m west along a straight path. Student 1 takes east as the positive direction; Student 2 takes west as the positive direction. Each finds the hiker's resultant displacement as a signed component. Which statement correctly compares their results?

options.text: Only Student 1 can be right, as east has to be the positive direction.
Student 1 gets −4 m and Student 2 gets +4 m, and both results mean 4 m west.
Both get +4 m, by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger.
Both get 14 m, since the two walks simply add to give the resultant.

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of mass 2m and length L has a small ball of mass m fixed to one end. How far from the other end of the rod is the centre of mass of the rod–ball system?

A uniform beam of length 5.0 m and weight 400 N rests horizontally on two supports, one at each end, P and Q. A person of weight 600 N stands on the beam 1.0 m from Q. What is the upward force from support P?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about Q: F_P × 5.0 = 400 × 2.5 + 600 × 1.0 = 1600 N m, so F_P = 320 N.

questions.stem: An ice cube floats in a glass of fresh water filled exactly to the brim. What happens as the ice melts completely?

options.text: Water overflows, because the part of the ice above the surface turns into extra water.
The level falls, because ice is less dense than water, so it shrinks as it melts.
The level stays the same, because the meltwater exactly fills the volume the ice displaced.
Water overflows only if more than half of the ice was above the surface.

questions.explanation: The floating ice displaces its own weight of water. When it melts, its mass is unchanged, so its meltwater takes up exactly the volume it was displacing.

questions.stem: An object moves along a straight line, with positive taken to the right. At one instant its velocity is −3.0 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is +2.0 m s⁻². The acceleration stays constant. Which describes the motion of the object?

options.text: Moving left and slowing down; it will then stop and stay at rest.
Moving left and speeding up, since its acceleration is positive.
Moving left and slowing down; later it will move off to the right.
Moving right and speeding up, in the direction of its acceleration.
